end.summary:
Recognised that halves use two equal parts, using a roti example.
Practised naming one-third of 15 pencils as one of three equal groups.
Confused numerator and denominator by comparing eaten or remaining parts with the total.
Identified equal sections in a watermelon and flag example.
Could not complete the teach-back; one-third of nine drumsticks was stated as three after prompting.
end.parentNote: Nisha practised recognising equal parts and naming halves, thirds, and quarters using rotis, pencils, fruit, flags, and drumsticks. They used the equal-groups method to find one-third of 15 and nine, and noticed that equal sections matter. There was a mix-up between parts taken or left and parts out of the whole; it was corrected for the one-third drumstick example, but the idea was not yet secure at the end. At home, share a roti or paper shape into 2, 3, or 4 equal parts and ask, “How many equal parts make the whole?” before naming one part.
